# Split the documentation: a smaller core cheat sheet and a web sheet
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #143, sha256:765099d21339fde1bd34727683326774b970ec4a5b5903f85da5b690b869818b). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** docs (thin slice; re-freezes the scored documentation)
- **Milestone:** Layered language: a domain-neutral core and one extension per domain
- **Source:** Steve's direction rulings relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-28 (web keywords belong in a web extension, not the core; look for clean breaks for other domains: desktop UI, mobile, data, testing, messaging, file IO, auth, background jobs) and Decider D89 (Codex No with conditions, Grok Support-it; the conditions are adopted). Agile: build only the web extension now; other domains when a real use needs them.
- **Depends on:** 142, 140
- **Story:** As Ari, I want the core cheat sheet to hold only domain-neutral language and a separate web sheet to hold the web constructs, so that a project loads only the documentation it uses.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given docs/CHEATSHEET.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md, When they are split, Then the core cheat sheet has no HTTP verbs, endpoint, route, status or respond-with text, a web cheat sheet (or index entry) holds them, every example still compiles with the real compiler, and the keyword coverage test of card 104 passes against the core sheet plus the web sheet
  2. Given the scored documentation, When the split lands, Then a Decider re-freezes the hashes of every documentation file and states that a fresh baseline is needed, and stored rows stay on the old baseline and are not rescored
  3. Given a project that uses web, When the documentation block is built for a model, Then it carries the core sheet and the web sheet and the token count of each is recorded
